common_name: Tally Ho Dahlia (Pale Orange Novelty Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed; the eye should point upward.

directions: Tally Ho holds an RHS Award of Garden Merit and sits in the catch-all Miscellaneous class because its pale-orange blooms don't fit the standard decorative, cactus, or ball forms. Its name borrows the old foxhunting cry, fitting for a flower whose irregular, almost tousled petals break from the tidy symmetry of show-bench dahlias. Stake plants early since the compact habit still carries a heavy flower load, and lift tubers before hard frost for replanting next season.

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep after soil has warmed following the last frost.

directions: Like Tally Ho, Waltzing Mathilda carries the RHS Award of Garden Merit while being filed under Miscellaneous rather than a standard bloom-shape class, its warm orange-and-pink petals twisting in a way that defies the usual decorative or cactus mold. The taller, well-branched habit makes it a reliable mid-border cut flower once established. Pinch the growing tip after planting to multiply flowering stems, and divide overwintered tubers every couple of years to keep clumps vigorous.

planting.note: Plant tubers 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed after the last frost.

directions: My-nute Blend is the third of only three dahlias the RHS files under its Miscellaneous award class, its blended orange-and-yellow petals giving a two-tone glow that standard decorative or cactus categories don't capture. Its compact, bushy habit suits containers or front-of-border planting better than the taller novelty dahlias bred for cutting. Deadhead spent blooms to extend flowering into autumn, and lift and store tubers over winter where the ground freezes.
